ironKey.name: Small iron key
ironKey.desc: Cold, and still caked with soil.

matchbox.name: Empty matchbox
matchbox.desc: The striking strip is still rough.

match.name: A single match
match.desc: Pressed flat, but the head looks dry.

birdKey.name: Winding key
birdKey.desc: A clock key with a little bird for a handle.

brassKey.name: Heavy brass key
brassKey.desc: Too big for anything in this room except the door.

glassEye.name: Glass eye
glassEye.desc: Grey-green. It seems to be looking at you.

combos.say: You strike the match. It burns with a small, very steady flame.

chapters.intro: A small room. The door won’t open, and it’s very dark.

do.text: The door won’t open. There’s a dial lock, and a keyhole under it.
The shadows step away from the door. Slowly.
You wind it. The clock starts ticking, very loudly.
Tiny clockmaker’s cutters, hidden behind the pendulum.
Just the pendulum now, swinging.
The pendulum case is shut tight. There’s no keyhole, only a tiny catch inside.
“If you’re reading this, the candle has gone out again. Don’t trust the window.”
“Whatever is written on the glass was written from the outside.”
It burns, but it doesn’t get any shorter.
A candle. The wick is still warm, as if someone just blew it out.
You wind it. The clock starts ticking, very loudly.
Stopped at quarter to four. There are two winding holes, but nothing to wind it with.
It’s ticking now. The hands can be turned from the winding holes.
Quarter past nine. It keeps ticking, but the hands don’t move on.
Her head has turned towards the clock. Her eyes are still painted shut.
Eleanor. Her eyes are painted shut.
One empty socket. She doesn’t seem to mind.
Her eyes are open now. One of them catches the light oddly.
Her left eye comes loose with a soft click. It’s glass.
Locked. The keyhole is very small.
An empty matchbox. The striking strip is still rough.
The chair in the photograph is empty now. Someone is standing at the window.
This room. Someone sits in a chair that isn’t here any more. The clock on the wall says quarter past nine.
A single match, pressed flat between the pages. Someone saved it for later.
You don’t want to put your hand in there again.
Dry soil. A loop of string pokes out of it.
The pocket is empty now. It’s still cold inside.
The cage is open now. Whatever lived here is gone.
A heavy key hangs from the perch, out of reach.
The little door is wired shut. Twisted tight, from the inside.
A heavy brass key. It’s warm, as if someone was holding it.
Someone has drawn on the glass with a finger. From the outside.
Black glass. You can’t even see your own reflection.
A small iron key on a string. Just before it came free, something under the soil pulled back.
Three knocks. From the other side of the door.
Sand pours out. Far more sand than a pocket could hold. Something fell out with it.
A winding key with a little bird for a handle. Somewhere, a clock has been waiting for it.
Somewhere in the room, a clock has been waiting for that winding key.

hints: Something is hidden in the plant pot.
Look closely at the soil by the window.
Pull the string poking out of the soil.
That iron key fits a small keyhole somewhere.
Look at the desk.
Select the iron key, then tap the drawer.
There’s a photograph in the drawer.
Look at it up close.
Tap the photograph in the drawer.
The drawer is open now.
Look inside it.
Take the matchbox.
Someone left their coat behind.
Check the coat’s pocket.
Tap the pocket, then pick up what falls out.

puzzles.inactiveSay: Nothing turns. The clock hasn’t been wound.

onSolve.text: The clock chimes. Below it, the pendulum case clicks open.

do.text: The coat is hanging on the other hook now.
Her head has turned. She’s facing the clock now.
The wick catches. Behind you, something in the room moves.
There’s someone standing just outside the door.
Everything in the room is waiting now. Even the clock.

hints: The clock has stopped.
The bird-shaped key belongs to the clock.
Select the winding key, then tap the clock face.
The clock wants a particular time.
The photograph shows the same clock.
Quarter past nine. The left hole turns the hours, the right hole the minutes.
Something opened below the clock.
Look at the pendulum case.
Tap the open pendulum case.
A matchbox is no use without a match.
One of the books looks different.
Open the red book on the shelf.
Two things you’re carrying belong together.
The match and the matchbox.
Tap one of them, then tap the other.
It’s very dark in here.
The candle on the desk.
Select the lit match, then tap the candle.

chapters.intro: The candle burns without getting any shorter. Now you can see what the dark was hiding.

A big, old keyhole under the dials.

Whispering, close to the window. It stops when you listen.
You turn around quickly. Nobody there.
The wire snaps. It was twisted shut from the inside.

The dials settle into place, but the door is still locked.

hints: Something is hanging inside the birdcage.
The cage door is wired shut.
Select the cutters, then tap the cage door.
The cage is open.
Take what’s inside it.
Tap the key hanging from the perch.
The door has a keyhole as well as dials.
The heavy brass key.
Select the brass key, then tap the door.
Light makes reflections.
Look closely at the window.
Look at the window now that the candle is lit.
The dials want four symbols.
Read the note on the desk, then look at the window again.
Moon, eye, key, bird.
The door is open.
Go through it.
Tap the open door.

endings.text: Behind you, the clock strikes quarter past nine again. In your pocket, the glass eye has gone warm.
Behind you, the clock strikes quarter past nine again. You have the feeling someone is still watching.
